comparison: Strong agreement on FRET data (C49-C55, C76, C86-C87). Both evaluations accept the FRET methodology and conclusions about N-terminal interactions between LRMP and HCN4. Peer reviewers highlight the rigorous spectroscopic analysis without raising methodological concerns.

Significant disagreement on mechanistic interpretation (C56-C58). OpenEval finds the mutagenesis data strongly supports the model, while peer reviewer sa3 questions whether P545/T547 are actually involved in the cAMP transduction center, stating the hypothesis 'awaits to be proven.' Both accept the data but differ on mechanistic conclusions.

Complete agreement on HCN4 N-terminus requirement (C39-C43, C75). Both evaluations accept the deletion series in Figure 3 without methodological concerns. Peer reviewers affirm the identification of the N-terminal domain as a binding domain for LRMP.

Strong agreement on gain-of-function experiment (C7, C64-C65). Both evaluations view the HCN2-4N chimera data as particularly compelling evidence. Peer reviewers specifically highlight Figure 7 as the study's highlight, confirming that N-terminus plus C-linker/S5 residues confer LRMP regulation to HCN2.

Partial disagreement on integrated mechanistic model (C8, C33, C78-C79, C89-C90). OpenEval finds the model well-supported by collective evidence. Peer reviewer sa3 challenges the specific allosteric mechanism through the transduction center, noting critical residues are not established as part of the cAMP transduction center in literature.

Strong agreement on core findings (C1, C2, C29). Both evaluations affirm the main conclusion that LRMP regulates HCN4 but not HCN2, with peer reviewers describing evidence as 'compelling' and 'convincing.' All reviewers explicitly support this central claim.

Complete agreement on LRMP domain mapping (C34-C38, C80). Both evaluations accept the progressive deletion analysis showing residues 1-227 are sufficient. Peer reviewers note the study shows 'initial 224 residues of LRMP are sufficient' without raising concerns about the functional data.

Agreement on LRMP mechanism distinct from TRIP8b (C30-C32, C92). Both evaluations accept that LRMP 1-479Cit regulates HCN4 without ER domains and that cAMP-dependent deactivation slowing is preserved, supporting the model that LRMP acts downstream of cAMP binding.

Agreement on C-terminal contributions (C44-C45, C48). Both evaluations accept the partial regulation of HCN4-S719X by LRMP, indicating the distal C-terminus contributes but is not essential. No methodological concerns raised by either evaluation.

Agreement on partial effects of mutations (C59-C60). Both evaluations accept the data showing partial regulation of HCN4-2, consistent with complex interactions between multiple domains and allosteric contributions of the distal C-terminus.

Agreement on control experiment (C46-C47). Both evaluations accept the HCN4-V604X result as an appropriate control showing CNBD requirement for cAMP binding. This is consistent with prior literature on similar truncations.

Agreement on negative control results (C61, C63). Both evaluations accept that C-linker and S5 mutations alone are insufficient, supporting the model that both N-terminus and C-linker/S5 regions are required for LRMP specificity.
OpenEval evaluates quantitative comparison of HCN4 vs HCN2 cAMP shifts (C66). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific quantitative observation.

OpenEval evaluates background claims and literature context (C9-C28, C67-C70, C74, C81-C85). Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these background/contextual claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates interpretations and speculative conclusions (C71-C73, C77, C91) as reasonable inferences. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these interpretive claims, though sa3's concerns about mechanism overlap with some of these claims.

Peer review evaluates claims C4, C5, and C72 regarding disordered N-terminus interactions. OpenEval addresses C72 in R13 as part of interpretive claims, but C4 and C5 are not explicitly grouped in OpenEval results, though related to findings in R3 and R5.

Peer review evaluates claim C3 (not specified in provided data) alongside LRMP domain mapping. OpenEval does not have a result specifically addressing C3, though R2 covers the related domain mapping claims.

Peer review evaluates claim C6 (not specified in provided data) alongside P545/T547 mutagenesis with uncertainty about mechanistic interpretation. OpenEval R6 addresses the same mutagenesis data (C56-C58) but finds it strongly supportive.
